The graph of the function $g(x)$ is shown above. 
Find the approximate ${g}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=4$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=0.5.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=3.5$ and $x=4.$*

${g}^{′}(4)≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{g}^{′}(x)≈\frac{g(x)-g(x-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $x=4.$ Applying the above formula with $x=4$ and $h=0.5$ gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(4) & ≈\frac{g(4)-g(4-0.5)}{0.5} \\  & =\frac{g(4)-g(3.5)}{0.5} \\  & =\frac{5-4}{0.5} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
